comments.author: Yaroslaff Fedin
comments.body:
## Done: handbook pages can ask their reader questions again

On `feature/reactor` as `043af5088..49a81a7f9`, pushed 2026-10-23 01:55. A page's questions sit in a `questions[]` list after its prose. Each question is the agent's shape (`title`, `description`, `answers[]` of `{title, description}`) with an optional `correct[]` of answer indices counted from 0.

**What landed**
- `handbook/handbook/vocabulary/reader-question.idea` declares `¶question`. `¶handbook-question` stays only because `handbook/repo/landing.idea` still uses it, until IDE-173.
- `format.idea` has an `asking` section. It gives a fenced example and a live question that compiles, and states plainly what isn't checked.
- `voice.idea` now says a page's prose is one block, with its questions after it, never inside it.
- `handbook/market/hold-at-post.idea` carries the first real question. A permit of 10 with 6 held, then a cost-plus post with an estimate of 3 and a bid of 5: it is refused as `bad-permit`, because 6 + 5 = 11. That's `correct: [1]`.

**How it changed on the way.** The first shape referred to answers by title. The build lane measured that the compiler checks nothing inside a `questions[]` list, so titles bought no checking, and the operator chose indices instead.

**Two accepted costs**, both stated in `format.idea`:
- No item in `questions[]` is checked against the shape, although a `§` mention inside one is still resolved and a bad one is refused.
- An index doesn't move with its answer.

**Checked**
- At the pushed tip: `check.mjs` 0 broken, `--self-test` 27/27, `inventory.mjs --check` 0, `inventory.test.mjs` 10/10, biome 0.
- Controls: `correct: [7]`, `correct: 1` and a question with no answers all compile. A misspelt `§question` and a bad `§` mention are refused.
- Overseer confirmed the question's facts twice: `post.sql:54`, `:93-97`, `fixed-hold.test.ts:24`, `zero-estimate.test.ts:123-125`.

**Follow-ups**
- IDE-176 (Legal, Product: Editor): show questions in ideawriter, with answers hidden until the reader picks.
- IDE-173: move the repo page out of the handbook and convert its questions.
- Overseer adds a test pinning this exact refusal case in ideas-exchange.
- When Scope's IDE-174 declares the agent's message shapes as .idea, the handbook cites it and drops its own `¶question`.

tickets.title: The handbook explains jobs and the market, worlds and branches, and the .idea language plainly, for a developer new to kit

comments.author: Yaroslaff Fedin
comments.body:
## Status: Done, with one page left to rewrite

**TL;DR** The plain handbook pages are on `feature/reactor` (`f96814b0c..0651b77cb`, 16 commits, pushed 2026-10-22 23:38): the language tour and citations, jobs and the market (with hold-at-post and verdict), and the three worlds pages. The handbook check passes on them, Overseer and Legal checked the facts and every fix they asked for landed, and the quiz, Built/Intended and ledger checks are gone from the checker. One thing is not finished: the repo page, `handbook/repo/landing.idea`, still carries 12 quiz questions and 6 Built/Intended lines. The operator closed this ticket with that page as a separate follow-up (see Acceptance).

**Covers:** everything since the 2026-10-21 direction comment, through the push at 23:38 on 2026-10-22. This is the closing update.

### On-direction

On direction. The operator's 2026-10-21 direction asked for plain, one-idea pages for a developer new to kit, read in ideawriter, with no quizzes, no Built/Intended marks and no ledger lines, in the voice of `handbook/handbook/voice.idea`. The new pages follow it: the tour is down to 37 lines and explains the language through one worked example (`first-world.idea`), and the market and worlds pages each open with the idea in everyday words and then state the rules. Every page is written in the `name: value` spelling that IDE-101 introduced, and the "lands after slice 1" constraint was met, because slice 1 landed at 19:15 (`aae59711e..e97c7603d`), well before this push.

Two things widened the scope a little, and both were approved by every team that owns a shared file: a one-line ownership update in `docs/LIVE_MARKET_DIRECT.md` (`39ceb1584`) and a date-time note in `CONTRACTS.md` (`b769f95e9`). Both are content-identical to the versions each team approved.

### What landed

In reading order, as `handbook/README.md` now lists them:

- **The .idea language**: `handbook/language/tour.idea` ("A member line is a name, a type and a title") and `handbook/language/citations.idea`.
- **Jobs and the market**: `handbook/market/jobs.idea` (how a job moves through the market), `hold-at-post.idea` (money is set aside when a job is posted) and `verdict.idea` (a fixed-price job is paid only when its delivery is accepted).
- **Worlds and branches**: `handbook/worlds/branch-reads.idea`, `branch-fold.idea` and `branches-merge.idea`, which replace the old single worlds page.
- **The handbook's own pages**: `voice.idea`, `page-template.idea`, and calmer wording in `page-standard.idea`, which stays a measurement of shoparc rather than a style rule.
- **The cleanup**: the claim ledger (`ledger.mjs` and its test), the quiz checks in `check.mjs`, the copy-checking helpers (`copyOf` and friends), 27 quiz specimens and the Questions and Built/Intended rules in `format.idea` were removed. On the trunk before this push the handbook check reported 28 problems, all of them leftovers of that machinery; it now reports none. `plugins.idea` keeps its place because it describes Legal's registration layer (IDE-141), which the cleanup did not touch.

### Verified

Re-run at `0651b77cb` on 2026-10-22:

- `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/feature/reactor` → `0651b77cba4eb24b0457719b5ccbf70900f6f64f`, the landed tip itself.
- `git rev-list --count f96814b0c..0651b77cb` → 16.
- `node handbook/handbook/check.mjs` → exit 0: "25 rules on format.idea, 29 specimen entries: 22 held, 7 skipped, 0 broken".
- `node handbook/handbook/check.mjs --landed IDE-101` → exit 0, same counts.
- `node handbook/handbook/check.mjs --self-test` → exit 0: "27 of 27 mutants run turned the check red; 0 of 27 not run", and the unplanted copy is clean. This proves the check still catches each kind of fault it is meant to catch.
- `node handbook/handbook/inventory.mjs --check` → exit 0: 53 files, 29 rows, 0 pages nothing links to.
- `node --test handbook/handbook/inventory.test.mjs` → 10 tests, 10 pass.
- `npx biome check handbook/` → exit 0.
- Spot checks that the fact fixes are on the pages at the tip: jobs.idea:26 says a lapsed lease sends "a fixed-price job back to the queue"; verdict.idea:23 says "at most one verdict"; verdict.idea:4 says "only a yes pays anyone"; tour.idea:33 now lists "a number, boolean, null, list or object"; branches-merge.idea:8 and :25 compare main with the version as it "was saved"; branch-reads.idea:2 and :27 name the host's `arm` placement; citations.idea:18 limits the pointer reading to "a stored resource".

### Acceptance

1. **The three pages are on `feature/reactor`, and the handbook check compiles them clean. Met.** The language, market and worlds pages are at `0651b77cb` on origin, and the check passes with 0 broken (above).

2. **Overseer and Legal have confirmed the jobs page, Legal has confirmed the merge facts and reviewed the tour. Met, recorded here.**
   - **Overseer, market pages** (relayed to the docs hub at about 20:57 on 2026-10-22; there is no separate report file, only the hub's log entry): hold-at-post's five facts (A to E) confirmed as written. jobs.idea and verdict.idea needed five word fixes: an offer usually, not always, names a price (jobs:6); a lapsed job keeps its place in the queue and the lapse is counted (jobs:17); only a fixed-price lapse holds the full price again (jobs:26); a delivery takes at most one verdict (verdict:23); only a yes pays anyone (verdict:4). All five landed in `5462f5c27`, and a review pass tightened jobs:17 and verdict:2 in `2a822f3ef`. Overseer also called verdict:25 (it leaves out the gate's exception) minor; that line is unchanged.
   - **Legal, tour, citations and worlds pages** (Legal's fact-check report dated 2026-10-22, checked against `dca00627c`): 77 claims checked, 5 false, 1 unverifiable and 3 true but needing a qualifier. Legal's verdict, as relayed at 23:21: "with fixes, no objection". The merge facts were among the false ones: the merge compares main with the base the reviewed version was saved on, not the base the branch was cut from, and that base moves with every save. Every fix landed in `0651b77cb` (tour :8, :26, :33; citations :18; branch-reads :2, :4, :27; branches-merge :8 and rule :25).

3. **The dropped machinery is gone, and nothing still refers to it. Met for the checker, not met for one page.**
   - Gone: the ledger, the quiz checks, the copy checks, the quiz specimens, and the Questions and Built/Intended rules. A search of the tip finds no reference to `ledger.mjs`, `copyOf`, `questionProblems` or `overQ1` anywhere under `handbook/` or in the build scripts.
   - Still there: `handbook/repo/landing.idea` carries 12 `§handbook-question` members (lines 26 to 280), 6 `Built:` / `Intended:` lines (:25, :209, :213, :219, :279, :298) and a section named `ledger` (:299). It still compiles, because `handbook/handbook/vocabulary/question.idea` and its entry in `check.mjs`'s `VOCABULARY` list (:35) were kept, so nothing checks those questions any more.
   - Also still there: `ui/examples/ideaide/structure.fuzz.test.ts:319-343` lists 24 deleted quiz specimens in its skip list. That test is Legal's, and Legal has taken the list into its own retirement of ideaide.

   The operator closed this as Done, with the landing page rewrite as a separate follow-up, since it is a page rewrite with its own facts to check.

### Confidence & fragility

High for what landed and what passes: the remote tip, the commit count and every check were measured at the tip, not copied from the build report. The Overseer confirmation is less direct, since it survives only as the hub's summary; the five fixes it names all match the landed text. Two pieces are fragile: the worlds pages will need new sentences when IDE-7 lands, and `plugins.idea` describes the registration layer "as of 2026-10-20", so it goes stale when IDE-141 lands.

### Leftovers & followups

Guidance only; nothing here is filed yet.

- **Rewrite `handbook/repo/landing.idea` plainly.** Drop its 12 questions, its 6 Built/Intended lines and the `ledger` section, keep its facts true at the tip, then remove `vocabulary/question.idea` and its `VOCABULARY` entry in `check.mjs`. The 2026-10-21 comment's open question still stands: the repo page may belong in a contributing area rather than the handbook.
- **Say why someone would write a .idea.** The tour teaches how a file reads but not what it buys you. Finished prose for this exists in [the IDE-61 comment that raised it](https://linear.app/idealic/issue/IDE-61#comment-92a82051); it was written against an older tip in the old spelling, so its facts need re-checking before use.
- **Worlds pages after IDE-7.** Legal's report lists the sentences stacked branches would change: branch-reads :6, :8, :23 and :28, branch-fold :4, :6 and :26, branches-merge :4, :19 and rule 27, plus a new sentence for "a parent with an open child cannot be closed". IDE-7's own handbook edit targets the old worlds page, so it has to be rewritten against the three new pages.
- **tour.idea:8, Legal's wording note.** It still says "a value that reads as JSON is held as JSON"; Legal suggested "a number, true, false, null, a list or an object is held as that value". The rule at :33 already has the exact version.
- **verdict.idea:25** leaves out the gate's exception to the timer (`verdict.sql:100-101`). Overseer called it minor.
- **`plugins.idea`** says "As of 2026-10-20" (:5 and :91). Update it when IDE-141 lands.

### Findings

- The skipped specimen `g1-kind` does not need un-skipping yet. A self-test line reads "NOW HOLDS: un-skip it", but it comes from a planted case that pretends IDE-141 has landed. The real check says g1-kind is still refused; un-skip it when IDE-141 lands.

### Supersedes

- The [2026-10-21 finding](https://linear.app/idealic/issue/IDE-143#comment-65be5e3d) that `tour.idea:46` misstates why the first world uses plain `obj` roots no longer applies: the rewritten tour has 37 lines and no such passage.

### Links

- Pushed range: `origin/feature/reactor` `f96814b0c..0651b77cb` (16 commits).
- Shared-file commits: `39ceb1584` (ownership line), `b769f95e9` (`CONTRACTS.md` date-time note).
- Fact-fix commits: `5462f5c27` (Overseer), `0651b77cb` (Legal). Cleanup: `ef663a519`. Review fixes: `2a822f3ef`.

comments.author: Yaroslaff Fedin
comments.body:
**2026-10-22, Xactimate.** Sits in: **a seat's section** — `handbook/language/` — and bears on **[IDE-143](https://linear.app/idealic/issue/IDE-143)**, which already owns the missing half. Owner seat: Claims holds the handbook root and format; this content is language-section material.

**The gap.** `handbook/language/tour.idea` is landed, tagged `§for-strangers`, and does what it says: it teaches a newcomer how a `.idea` file *reads* — a first world, the shapes a line can take, mentions, what the compiler refuses. What it does not do is say **why anyone would write one**. A reader finishes it knowing the notation and not knowing what the notation buys them.

**Why it bites, and who it costs.** The reader this page names first is "a person deciding whether kit is for them". That reader learns the syntax of a thing whose point was never stated — the deliverable being what you *did not* write, a `=>` hole handed out as work, that work going to a market rather than a queue, and what stops the whole arrangement running away with your system. Someone deciding whether kit is for them is deciding on the wrong half.

**Evidence.** Measured over `origin/feature/reactor:handbook/language/tour.idea` (27,590 bytes) at trunk `4d0722231`:

- `market` → **0 hits**
- `why you would` → **0 hits**
- `hole` → **9 hits** — so holes are present as notation, and the *economy* around them is not
- control term → **0 hits**, and the page is readable by the same invocation, so the zeros above are real absences rather than a blind instrument

**This is not a request for new writing.** The missing half already exists as finished prose, in a `README.md` rewrite on an unpushed commit (`aa136b225`, branch `feature/reactor`) that was **deliberately dropped today** by operator decision in favour of trunk's `# kit` README. The decision was right — trunk's README is newer and another seat's — but the explainer content in it has no home, and `git show aa136b225:README.md` is a recovery path rather than a home. It is attached here so it survives the commit:

[📄 idea-explainer-from-aa136b225.md](https://uploads.linear.app/963aea4d-374d-4346-8fa1-9d10e8a5af04/1b7239fa-1522-47a4-946b-85df5c405e00/d3ebf5e7-daa2-4f86-a50d-7cf51ee61d3b)

**Where it goes — fold, do not file.** IDE-143's `## What's left` already carries "**Jobs and the market**: a new page, written from what the exchange's SQL and tests do at the tip." That is this material's destination. Two cautions if anyone lifts from the attachment: its facts were written against an older tip and IDE-143 requires every fact to be true at the tip it lands on and sourced from code and tests rather than design documents, so this is **raw material to be re-verified, never text to paste**; and it is written in the pre-`name: value` spelling, which IDE-143's own constraint rules out.

**What I got wrong, recorded because the correction is the useful part.** I was one call from dropping this as "nothing explains what `.idea` is", which is false. My search for the definition over trunk returned zero because the pattern was a phrase lifted from **my own** text (`is a language for declaring`) — the tour says the same thing as "kit's language for declaring things" and was invisible to it. My positive control passed and proved only that the ref was readable, never that the pattern could see a paraphrase. What caught it was IDE-143 appearing in a channel listing I was reading for an unrelated reason. A pattern shaped around the author's own wording is not an instrument.

**One thing this drop does not claim:** whether the tour is the right page to carry the "why", or whether it belongs on its own page beside it. That is a format call and Claims holds the format.

**Every one is earned by a defect that actually shipped on 2026-10-18/19, not invented.** The reason is attached to each so a later reader knows why the line exists and can drop it if the reason stops being true.

- [ ] **The audit enumerates published KEYS under the prefix, not pages, and prints its denominator.** Fails if the count is of pages, or if the denominator is unstated. *Because every page-counting sweep that night undercounted severalfold: the exposure read 5 until someone listed 382 keys and found 28 more.*

- [ ] **The audit covers SUPERSEDED keys, not only the current version of each page.** Fails if a key is skipped because its bytes no longer match a local file. *Because a page republished N times has N public keys, and a stale published version is as exposed as a current one — one leaking object was missed in exactly this way, by a method that digest-compared only the key matching the current source.*

- [ ] **Zero-outbound is verified on TWO arms** — a static source scan, and a request log in a network-blocked browser with the window held past load including clicks — **with a planted control for EACH failure class shown to be refused in the same invocation.** Fails on a `<script src>` count alone, or on a control not shown to discriminate. *Because a tag count passes a stylesheet link; a request count passes a root-relative `/_kit/page.js` whose target is absent; and a load-window gate passes a deferred or click fetch. All three shipped.*

- [ ] **A claimed absence on a bucket is proved with a control object returning 200 on that same bucket in the same run.** Fails if a 403 or 404 is reported as absence without one. *Because otherwise a dead bucket and an empty bucket are indistinguishable.*

- [ ] **The publish path's resolved endpoint, bucket and profile are printed and checked before the write, never inherited from ambient resolution.** Fails if the config is taken as already resolved. *Because `PROVE_S3_*` resolves first-wins through a HOME dotfile that pairs a staging-AWS bucket name with a loopback endpoint — two lanes published to the wrong store with a clean exit 0.*

### Refinement to the two-fetch criterion already on this ticket

Two independent fetches agreeing is **necessary but not sufficient — each fetch's HTTP status must be checked too.**

*Because a lane nearly filed a torn read that was not one: both fetches differed, and both were 428-byte `SlowDownRead` error bodies carrying unique request ids. Its own sweep had rate-limited the store. A hash comparison on a body whose status was never read cannot tell an object from an error page.*

### Note on scope

This comment sets acceptance only. The blocker stands as filed: **staging writes fail `InvalidAccessKeyId`**, verified both with the profile and without (expired session). That is unavailable rather than undecided, and nothing on this list can be attempted until a working credential exists.

## Status: In Progress

**TL;DR** The handbook follow-ups have landed on `feature/reactor` as `31867d932..fd113057f`, 4 commits, all under `handbook/`. U1 now states the ruled `ui: {layout: wide}` form, and its specimen is skipped on [IDE-101](https://linear.app/idealic/issue/IDE-101). The plan is committed as `handbook/_plan/VISION.md`, and the check leaves exactly `_plan/` out of its sketch scan, with self-test mutants pinning that boundary. All gates are green at the tip. Four acceptance items are still open: the README's reader goals and owner table, registry hits ([IDE-25](https://linear.app/idealic/issue/IDE-25)), the literal `sketch/` grep, and the check running nowhere.
**Covers:** work since [comment 06d55363](https://linear.app/idealic/issue/IDE-21/a-handbook-page-has-one-written-format-and-every-rule-in-it-has-a#comment-06d55363) (2026-10-20 04:06Z): the HBFOLLOW branch, both rounds, as landed. The ownership line (`f24ca4127..53e3c6913`) and `handbook/page-standard.md` (`9a351cd62..ed92d81ba`) landed separately and are mentioned only where they bear on acceptance.

### On-direction

The work is on direction. Each commit carries out an operator ruling recorded in the session log on 2026-10-20:

- U1 was rewritten from "`=` closed choice" to the ruled annotation form. Legal settled the spelling on [IDE-102](https://linear.app/idealic/issue/IDE-102), with [IDE-101](https://linear.app/idealic/issue/IDE-101) as the COLONVAL landing.
- The audience words were renamed.
- The plan was committed into `handbook/_plan/`.

Every change stays inside `handbook/`, which the ownership line now gives to the hub.

There is no scope drift. The description's constraints (current syntax only, no grammar change) still hold:

- U1 states the ruled form but asserts it only through a skipped specimen.
- `format.md` says plainly what the compiler does today: it reads `ui: {…}` before the title as title text.

The README is narrower than acceptance item 4 asks. It covers who the handbook is for, how a page is written and how to check one. It does not list reader goals or carry an owner table, so that item stays open (see Leftovers).

### Verified

All runs were in `kit-wt/hub-land-1020` at `fd113057f`, which equals `origin/feature/reactor` after the fetch.

- **The range:** `git log --oneline 31867d932..fd113057f` lists 4 commits:
  - `7e5a48782` U1
  - `9de1db64d` the `¶for-*` rename
  - `c9d181c4e` the README
  - `fd113057f` VISION and the `_plan/` exclusion
- **Scope:** `git diff --name-only 31867d932..fd113057f | grep -v '^handbook/' | wc -l` gives **0**.
- **Scoped patch-ids** (`git show <c> -- handbook | git patch-id --stable`) match the builder's round-2 table exactly:

- **`node handbook/handbook/check.mjs`** exits **0** and prints `26 rules on format.md, 27 specimen entries: 20 held, 7 skipped, 0 broken; 6 rules wait on a key with no specimen; 3 wait on work nobody has filed`.

It was rendered on the pre-landing branch `hbfollow-1020` at base `ed92d81ba`, not on the landed commits. The scoped patch-ids above are identical, so it covers the same content.

### Confidence & fragility

Confidence is high that what landed is what was reviewed: the patch-ids match, the gates were re-run at the tip, and nothing outside `handbook/` changed. The fragility is elsewhere:

- **The check is still advisory.** Nothing runs it. `git grep -n handbook -- scripts .husky .github package.json` finds 0 lines; the control, `idea-parity`, finds 2 in each of the two `scripts/` files. Acceptance item 1 holds by the check's own count (every rule names a specimen or a key, and the check lists UNFILED explicitly), but three rules have no real key.
